newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FLOODED CZECH LANDS NOW FIGHT MOSQUITO BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: FLOODED CZECH LANDS NOW FIGHT MOSQUITO BATTLE.

text.p: People in the eastern Czech Republic, slogging through mud left by the worst flooding of the century, now must contend with a massive infestation of mosquitoes, the local CTK news agency reported on Tuesday.
It quoted health officials in the Moravian district capital of Olomouc as saying that some people were being attacked by more than 100 mosquitoes per minute.
Although chemical insecticides were being used to limit the concentration in some areas, the infestation could last until colder weather comes in September, they said.

The pests are further complicating the massive cleanup in hundreds of cities and towns throughout the east and north of the country where floods were blamed for at least 49 deaths, destroying homes, crops and businesses.
While flood waves still pushed downstream on the Oder river in Poland and Germany, Czech rivers continued to recede on Tuesday.
The worst of the flooding in the Czech Republic was caused by torrential rains in the first two weeks of July.

President Vaclav Havel took a break from his summer holiday to visit some of the flooded areas nearby on Tuesday, visiting a machine shop which said it was facing liquidation because of damages from the flood.

Damage estimates in the Czech Republic range between 50 to 100 billion crowns. The government has authorised about 13 billion crowns in state relief aid, including the issuance of domestic flood relief bonds.
